latin: Qui intellexerit in dextrali coordinatione subordinationem pietatis ad sapientiam, perfecte intelliget_per uiam Cabalae quomodo Abraam in die suo per rectam lineam uidit diem Christi, et gauisus est.
latin_note: The underscore in 'intelliget_per' reproduces an OCR artifact for a word-space in the corpus copy (farmer1998:27217).
translation: Whoever will have understood, in the right-hand ordering, the subordination of piety to wisdom will fully understand, by way of the Cabala, how Abraham in his day, by a straight line, saw the day of Christ, and rejoiced.
translation_note: The allusion is to John 8:56 ('Abraham... saw my day, and was glad'); Farmer glosses 'piety' and 'wisdom' as the fourth and second sefirot respectively, correlated here with 'the day of Abraham' and 'the day of Christ' (farmer1998:27242).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch19, from Latin at farmer1998:27217
doctrine: Farmer glosses 'piety' and 'wisdom' as the fourth and second sefirot, correlated with 'the day of Abraham' and 'the day of Christ', and identifies Christ's association with divine 'Wisdom' with 1 Corinthians 1:24; he glosses the 'right-hand order' as the sefirot proper, as against an 'emanation of the left-hand' composed of evil forces (farmer1998:27242). He cross-references the thesis to 11>29, on the Cabalists' 'green line' that girds the universe, and to 25.7, on the threefold nature signified by the direct, reflected, and refracted ray in the science of optics (farmer1998:27012, 17003).
historiography: Wirszubski quotes the thesis's Latin in full twice: first introducing it as 'Pico's thirty-seventh thesis' that 'bears out my conclusion' (wirszubski1989:7057), and again designating it 'Conclusio xxxvii' in a passage on how Christian Kabbala is created through the superposition of the symbolic language of Jewish Kabbala upon an eminently Christian text (wirszubski1989:8518, 8520).
